subject: Capacity preflight — ThermoSys concurrency & response-profile worksheet
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@thermosys.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@thermosys.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ThermoSys preflight data for Dedicated POC

Hi Dylan / Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency guarantees and the fallback model routing. We are preparing a short POC and want to confirm the dedicated capacity footprint and the likely GPU mix. To help you size, I attached a small sample of our traffic and a one-page SLA rundown. Can you confirm what else you need?

Quick details (high level):
- Use case: real-time code-assist and short-document summarization for enterprise users
- Expected active users during POC: 800 users (80 concurrent on avg, peak bursts up to ~1,600 for short windows)
- Typical prompt length: 80–180 tokens (mostly instructions + code snippet)
- Typical completion length: 40–250 tokens (varies by task)
- Desired p99 latency for interactive flows: <= 350ms (token-by-token streaming ok)

Attached: thermosys_traffic_sample.csv (10-minute sample), ThermoSys_SLA_Rundown.pdf

Specific asks from our side:
1) Proposed GPU SKUs and estimated number of cards for the POC (2-week window)
2) Expected cost range (committed vs burst)
3) Any config we should change in our prompts to reduce tail latency/cost (batching tolerance, tokenization tips)

If helpful, Samir and I can join a quick 30-minute sizing call.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, ThermoSys
alyssa@thermosys.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@thermosys.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2024 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ThermoSys preflight data for Dedicated POC

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the sample and the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (pre-sales capacity lead) and Vivek (inference infra) for sizing.

High level: we can usually meet a ~350ms p99 for interactive code-assist with a mixed GPU pool + KV prefix caching, but the exact footprint depends on: tokenization variance, prompt/response distribution (we saw that in your sample), and whether you can accept short prefix-caching windows for code contexts.

Before we run a short throughput simulation, two clarifying questions:
- For the 1,600 peak bursts, how long do those bursts typically last? (seconds / minutes)
- Do your users open multiple parallel LLM sessions (one per tab/session) or is it single session with higher QPS?

Action plan (suggested):
1) You provide a 1-hour higher-resolution sample (top-of-hour traffic) OR confirm burst duration — we can extrapolate.
2) We run a 24-hr micro-sim using your sample + synthetic prompt/response mixes (we'll return an SKU mapping and estimated # of cards).
3) Follow-up call to review recommended Dedicated config and cost delta for reserved vs. burst.

I booked tentative 30 min on Friday — feel free to move.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Alyssa Turner <alyssa@thermosys.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2024 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ThermoSys preflight data for Dedicated POC

Alyssa / team — a few quick notes from the infra side that will speed up sizing and tighten cost estimates:

1) Concrete numbers we need in the sample (if you can include):
   - per-request token counts (input vs output) as raw integers (not just percentiles)
   - timestamped QPS at 1s granularity for a 10–15 minute window around expected peak
   - any client-side retry/backoff behavior (retries inflate concurrency)

2) Latency SLOs and tolerances: is 350ms p99 a hard cut (we assume yes) or is a 450ms p99 acceptable if it halves the SKU count?

3) Config levers we plan to try in the micro-sim:
   - KV cache for repeated prompts (code completions where prefix repeats)
   - Aggressive token quantization candidate (int8) for non-PII workloads to reduce memory pressure
   - Dynamic batching tuned for 95th pct sequence length to keep tail latency within SLO while saving cost on avg.

4) Preliminary SKU suggestion for the POC (very rough, pending sim):
   - 6 x A10G-equivalent for baseline with autoscale to 10 cards during short peak windows OR
   - 4 x H100-equivalent for lower latency/pack density if you opt for a 24/7 reserved commit (higher unit cost but smaller card count).

I'll run the micro-sim once we have the higher-res sample — should take ~48 hrs to generate a recommended mapping and cost bands.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Infra / Pre-sales, Redwood Inference
